evaluations.evidence: As a moderator, I want to create a new game by entering a name and an optional description
evaluations.rationale: Creating a game is a self-contained feature and does not require any other backlog story to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: invite estimators by giving them a URL where they can access the game
evaluations.rationale: Inviting via a game URL inherently requires that a game (and its URL) can be created first (PP-001).

evaluations.evidence: start a round by entering an item
evaluations.rationale: Starting a round requires an existing game/session context (a game must have been created), so it depends on PP-001.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Viewing the items for a session presumes a game/session exists (created via PP-001) and an items list tied to that session.

evaluations.evidence: select an item to be estimated or re-estimated
evaluations.rationale: Selecting an item requires that items exist (i.e., an item-add/import feature), so it depends on adding items to the session (PP-006) and the session itself (PP-001).

evaluations.evidence: add an item to the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Adding items must occur within a game/session context, so it depends on the ability to create a game (PP-001).

evaluations.evidence: edit an item in the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Editing presumes items already exist (added or imported), so it depends on item-creation/import features (e.g., PP-006) and a game/session (PP-001).

evaluations.evidence: delete an item from the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Deleting an item requires items to exist and a session to contain them, so it depends on item creation (PP-006) and the game (PP-001).

evaluations.evidence: show all estimates immediately
evaluations.rationale: Changing reveal behavior presumes the ability to collect estimates and the presence of estimators (join/estimate features), so it depends on joining/estimating stories (e.g., PP-002 and PP-029 / PP-033).

evaluations.evidence: accept the average of all estimates
evaluations.rationale: Accepting an average requires estimates to be collected and visible, so it depends on estimate-collection/reveal behavior (PP-033) and participant estimating (PP-034).

evaluations.evidence: "estimate" field filled in automatically if all estimators show the same card
evaluations.rationale: Auto-fill based on all estimators showing the same card presumes estimator participation and reveal logic, so it depends on join/estimating stories (PP-029, PP-034) and reveal behavior (PP-033).

evaluations.evidence: enter the agreed-upon estimate
evaluations.rationale: Entering an agreed estimate to move on presumes rounds/estimate fields and round control exist (start/round management), so it depends on starting a round (PP-003).

evaluations.evidence: estimate a story we estimated earlier in the session again
evaluations.rationale: Re-estimating an earlier story requires access to prior-round data (scroll/back or history in-session), so it depends on the ability to view prior rounds (PP-039) and round management (PP-003).

evaluations.evidence: import stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Importing stories targets a game's item list, so it requires a game/session context and an items list (PP-001 and PP-006).

evaluations.evidence: copy/paste stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Copy/paste will populate a game's items list and therefore presumes a game/session and item storage; depends on PP-001 and PP-006.

evaluations.evidence: browse through previous games
evaluations.rationale: Browsing previous games presumes games are created and stored (PP-001) before this feature can be used.

evaluations.evidence: view a transcript of a game
evaluations.rationale: Viewing a game transcript requires stored games/transcripts and likely browsing/searching (PP-016) and creation/storage of games (PP-001).

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a HTML file
evaluations.rationale: Exporting a transcript requires the transcript/viewing capability (PP-017) to exist first.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a CSV file
evaluations.rationale: Similar to PP-018, exporting a transcript in CSV requires the transcript/viewing feature (PP-017).

evaluations.evidence: delete a game
evaluations.rationale: Deleting a game presumes games exist (created/stored) and a way to select them (browsing previous games PP-016), so it depends on PP-001 and PP-016.

evaluations.evidence: create an account for the application by entering my name, email address, a password and a username
evaluations.rationale: Account creation is a self-contained feature and does not inherently depend on other backlog stories.

evaluations.evidence: log in using my account name and password
evaluations.rationale: Login requires accounts to exist (PP-021), so it depends on the account-creation story.

evaluations.evidence: change my account details
evaluations.rationale: Changing account details requires an existing account and typically the ability to authenticate (PP-021 and PP-022).

evaluations.evidence: delete my account
evaluations.rationale: Deleting an account requires an account to exist (PP-021) and likely requires authentication (PP-022).

evaluations.evidence: see dates and times in my local timezone
evaluations.rationale: Timezone display is a presentation/formatting feature and does not inherently depend on other backlog stories.

evaluations.evidence: get a password reminder by email
evaluations.rationale: Password reminder presumes an account with an email exists (PP-021), so it depends on account creation.

evaluations.evidence: select whether to have the team estimate with {..Fibonacci..} or {..powers of 2..}
evaluations.rationale: Selecting estimate scales is a per-game moderator action and presumes a game/session context (PP-001) in which to set this option.

evaluations.evidence: invite up to 15 estimators
evaluations.rationale: This refines invitation behavior and thus depends on the invite mechanism (PP-002) and game creation (PP-001).

evaluations.evidence: join a game by entering my name on the page I received the URL for
evaluations.rationale: Joining via a received URL presumes that a game and invitation URL have been created (PP-002) and thus depends on PP-002 (and implicitly PP-001).

evaluations.evidence: see the item we're estimating
evaluations.rationale: Seeing the current item requires rounds/items to be displayed (start round PP-003) and being participant in the game (join PP-029).

evaluations.evidence: see all items we will try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: For an estimator to view the session's items, a game/session and item list must exist (PP-001 and PP-006) and the estimator must join (PP-029).

evaluations.evidence: immediately see that an estimate has been given by a specific estimator
evaluations.rationale: This requires estimator presence (join PP-029) and the mechanism to submit/track estimates (PP-034/PP-041), so it depends on those stories.

evaluations.evidence: be shown all estimates at the same time after all estimators have given their estimate
evaluations.rationale: The simultaneous reveal behavior presumes estimator submission and detection of 'all estimators given' (PP-029 and PP-034/PP-041), so it depends on those stories.

evaluations.evidence: be able to change my estimate up until the last person selects a card and all are shown
evaluations.rationale: This participant behavior assumes the ability to join and submit estimates (PP-029) and the draw/reveal mechanism (PP-033), so it depends on those features.

evaluations.evidence: see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated
evaluations.rationale: Showing prior estimates requires storage/history and navigation through prior rounds (PP-039) and participants having submitted estimates (PP-034), so it depends on PP-039 and PP-034.

evaluations.evidence: see who gave what estimates during the current round
evaluations.rationale: Identifying who gave which estimates requires join/identity (PP-029) and reveal/tracking of estimates (PP-033/PP-032), so it depends on those stories.

evaluations.evidence: be able start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see
evaluations.rationale: A shared timer presumes multiple participants and real-time session context (join/ session - PP-029 and PP-001), so it depends on PP-029 (and implicitly PP-001).

evaluations.evidence: two-minute timer reset itself as soon as we all play an estimate
evaluations.rationale: Auto-reset requires the timer feature (PP-037) and detection of all estimators having played (PP-033), so it depends on PP-037 and PP-033.

evaluations.evidence: scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds
evaluations.rationale: Viewing prior rounds requires that prior rounds and their estimates are recorded (depends on starting rounds PP-003 and estimate submission PP-034), so it depends on those stories.

evaluations.evidence: always have the cards in the same order across multiple draws
evaluations.rationale: Card ordering is a UI/behavioral requirement that is self-contained and does not inherently require other backlog stories.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed
evaluations.rationale: Changing estimates presumes being an estimator in a session (join PP-029) and the draw/reveal mechanism (PP-033), so it depends on those features.

evaluations.evidence: have a small thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played
evaluations.rationale: Displaying a user's thumbnail typically depends on user account/profile data (PP-021) or an avatar feature, so it depends on account creation (PP-021).

evaluations.evidence: have written a site which is compliant with XHTML and CSS standards
evaluations.rationale: Standards compliance is a developer-level, standalone requirement and does not require other backlog stories.

evaluations.evidence: have a list of definitions for commonly used terms
evaluations.rationale: A glossary/definitions list is self-contained and does not inherently depend on other backlog stories.

evaluations.evidence: have created database indexes
evaluations.rationale: Creating indexes is a technical task that does not inherently require other backlog user stories to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: have the application function correctly in Internet Explorer 6 and 7, Firefox 1.5 and 2, and Safari 2
evaluations.rationale: Cross-browser support is a non-dependent quality requirement and does not inherently rely on other backlog stories.

evaluations.evidence: have the site comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines where possible
evaluations.rationale: Accessibility compliance is a standalone quality objective not inherently dependent on other backlog stories.

evaluations.evidence: have the application respond quickly to my actions
evaluations.rationale: Performance requirements are independent non-functional requirements and do not inherently require specific other stories.

evaluations.evidence: be able to use Unicode
evaluations.rationale: Unicode support is a self-contained technical requirement and does not inherently depend on other backlog stories.

evaluations.evidence: see sensible and predictable URLs
evaluations.rationale: URL design is a standalone UI/UX requirement and not inherently dependent on other backlog stories.

evaluations.evidence: have nice error pages when something goes wrong
evaluations.rationale: Error page design is self-contained and does not inherently depend on other user stories.

evaluations.evidence: results to be stored in a non-identifiable way
evaluations.rationale: Storing results presumes that results/games are captured and persisted (game creation and storage PP-001 and transcript/storage features), so it depends on PP-001 and related storage stories.

evaluations.evidence: be able to see some metrics on use of the game
evaluations.rationale: While metrics require data collection, this is a standalone analytics feature and does not explicitly require another specific backlog story to be implemented first.
